# 20. Conclusion

O-CPS is not an attempt to displace the existing cooperative-perception standards ecosystem. It is a composition of that ecosystem into a single opinionated profile that is implementable today on current radio hardware, auditable against a public reference, and publishable under a license posture that forecloses rent-seeking around the base protocol.

What distinguishes this specification from the existing state of the art is not novelty in any single layer. It is the combination of: a normalized perception profile that makes heterogeneous sensor suites interoperable at the message layer; a continuous-attestation model that makes trust a real-time signal rather than a certificate-issuance event; a driver-authority-absolute posture in every cooperative behavior; and an explicit refusal to introduce cloud dependencies into safety-critical paths.

The standards ecosystem around cooperative perception is crowded. What it has been missing is a composition layer with opinions. This document is that layer. It is offered to implementers, road authorities, and standards bodies as a shared target rather than as a product to be purchased.
